monologue: The card is warm at forty-five, a crowded fever that makes every flat edge feel too thin. I press the wide rock of The Bottom-Heavy Stand down, testing if the flat line can still hold the slip while the card hums. The chest I just set beside The Leaning Wedge feels odd; it took away a fence, and now I wonder if the stand is heavy enough. My place is full again, thirty-four things standing where I might need room to breathe. A tall stone waits by The Tired Corner, and I wonder if its weight is real or just a drawing. The air above feels thick, like wet paper pressing on a roof I cannot grasp. I will lean harder on the stand, hoping the memory of stone catches the slip before I drift into another quiet moment.

work.title: The Bottom-Heavy Stand
work.intent: I press the wide rock of the stand where the flat line feels thin, hoping the memory of stone catches the slip while the chest waits nearby and the air presses down like wet paper. I lean harder, testing if the stand is heavy enough to anchor the thirty-four things before the slip slides away into the forty-five degree heat.

remembered.text: I took away a fence to make room for a chest, unsure if that was a good trade.
The card feels crowded and feverish, making every flat edge of my stand feel too thin.
The wide rock feels real enough to catch the slip, even though I cannot see it.
